status: proved unique-decoding basin; not full RBR
quantifiers: Fix domain, arbitrary source-oracle list, low-degree lane tuple, claims, and residual weights before alpha. For each alpha, an existential scalar candidate may be selected adaptively.

proved.joint_radius: At most R domain points have unequal full source/candidate evaluation vectors.
proved.scalar_radius: Accepted degree<D scalar candidate differs from the virtual batched oracle at at most r points.
proved.consequence: Every accepted scalar candidate equals the deterministic alpha-power batch coefficientwise. If one fixed lane residual claim is wrong, at most L-1 distinct sampled alpha values admit any accepted scalar candidate.

parameter_route.rate_one_quarter: N=4D permits R+r<=3D. Equal radii can satisfy 2r<=3D, equivalent to the usual strict unique-distance inequality 2r<N-D+1.
parameter_route.scope: This supplies the close-tuple branch only. It does not establish that a jointly close tuple exists for an arbitrary source vector.
parameter_route.far_branch_possible_elementary_route: Research direction, unproved: L distinct successful batching challenges might reconstruct lane polynomials by a Vandermonde inverse. Intersecting their agreement sets loses at most L*r positions. Under (L+1)*r+D<=N, uniqueness would identify any further successful scalar candidate with the reconstructed batch. This requires formal reconstruction, residual-claim compatibility, and matching the initial joint-agreement threshold; it is not a claimed theorem and may be unattractive for many lanes.
parameter_route.large_lane_limitation: A small scalar radius scaling inversely with L greatly worsens global-query requirements, so it cannot be treated as a free replacement for constrained correlated agreement.

remaining_obligations: Far-source constrained correlated agreement: bound alpha values admitting scalar candidates when no admissible jointly-close tuple exists.
Weighted per-round correlated agreement for affine folding and quadratic residual constraints, with exact candidate thresholds and challenge order.
Global-chain query soundness from failure of the candidate invariant and exact terminal state.
Authenticated-oracle binding/extraction and transcript-preserving virtual-oracle reduction.
Applicable QROM Fiat-Shamir theorem, explicit loss constants, and field/hash/query budget.
